title: Normalization and Denormalization: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Normalization and Denormalization: Visual Guide

1. The Dependency Map | four functional dependencies of a flat order_lines table, each showing whether its left side is the key and how many copies of the right side that creates | redundancy appears exactly where a dependency's left side is not a key, which is the one rule behind every normal-form violation

2. Key, Whole Key, Nothing But | the same table stepped from 0NF through 1NF, 2NF and 3NF, splitting into four tables, with unit_price deliberately left behind | 1NF gives atomic values, 2NF removes partial dependencies on a composite key, 3NF removes transitive ones, but the real question is which entity a fact describes

3. Three Anomalies | update, insertion and deletion scenarios run against the flat schema and the 3NF one, with a slider for how far an 812-row UPDATE got before dying | normalization makes inconsistency structurally unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged, because each fact is a single-row atomic write

4. Paying Storage For Reads | a read-volume slider comparing a join shuffled on every query against one nightly join plus a dictionary-encoded stored column, with the three safety conditions | denormalization is an arithmetic argument that only holds when reads dominate, a normalized record persists upstream, and refresh is automated and idempotent

5. Three Shapes | one order with three lines stored normalized, flat wide, and as ARRAY<STRUCT>, scored on duplication, read cost and write cost | nesting pre-materializes the join without duplicating parent columns and UNNEST restores child grain, at the cost of rewriting the whole parent row to change one element
